haiku-low.q1: A pull request builds the image and runs make test-unit only, with no push, deploy or announce. A merge to main starts a run that can deploy.
haiku-low.q2: Staging and production deploy the same image, registry.internal/shop-api:<merged commit SHA>, built once in step 1. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: An integration test failure gets one automatic retry, then ends the run and is announced if it still fails. A unit test failure has no retry, ends the run and is announced.
haiku-low.q4: Staging keeps running the image from previous_tag after deploy.sh rollback staging. The schema is not rolled back. The image is found via SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag.
haiku-low.q5: Any member of the release-approvers group, except the author of the merged commit. If nobody approves within 72 hours, the run expires, nothing goes to production, and the expiry is announced.
haiku-low.q6: In AWS Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. Only deploy.sh writes them, and only after a rollout succeeds. The canary is never recorded.
haiku-low.q7: Stable keeps working on its existing image, and the recorded tags are unchanged because the canary is never recorded. The schema may have changed from the canary migration and is not undone.
haiku-low.q8: It stops quietly as superseded and is not announced, provided it has not yet taken the production lock.
haiku-low.q9: Outside the window, it releases the production lock, waits for the next window, then tries again. If another production deploy holds the lock, it waits for that lock.
haiku-low.q10: Measured: canary 5xx ratio over the last minute, from Prometheus. The run queries every 30 seconds for 15 minutes, from one minute after rollout. Failure: any sample above 1%, or no data.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED. The document says only that CI records who approved and when. It does not say how approvers are notified or what information they receive.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED as an automatic return. The document says no rollback is called after a failed stable rollout, because previous_tag may name an older image. Kubernetes keeps serving old pods, and a person decides.

sonnet.q1: A pull request only builds the image and runs make test-unit; it never pushes, deploys or announces. A merge to main starts a run that can deploy.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy registry.internal/shop-api:<tag>, where tag is the full commit SHA of the merged commit. The image is built once in step 1 and nothing is rebuilt later.
sonnet.q3: An integration test failure gets one automatic retry, and if it still fails the run ends and is announced. A unit test failure gets no retry, so the run ends and is announced. Both must pass.
sonnet.q4: The run calls deploy.sh rollback staging, which puts staging back on previous_tag (read from SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag). The schema is not rolled back. The run then ends and is announced.
sonnet.q5: A member of the release-approvers group, but not the author of the merged commit (that approval is discarded and the job keeps waiting). If nobody approves within 72 hours the run expires, nothing goes to production, and the expiry is announced in #deploys.
sonnet.q6: In AWS Parameter Store (SSM) as /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. Only deploy.sh writes them, and only after a rollout succeeds. The canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: The run calls deploy.sh canary-off, then fails and announces. Stable is unchanged and keeps serving, the SSM tags are unchanged because the canary is never recorded, and the schema may already have changed (migrations are never undone) but stable still works because every migration must work with the previous image.
sonnet.q8: The older run is superseded: it stops quietly (not announced), provided it has not yet taken the production lock. It checks while waiting for approval, the window or the production lock.
sonnet.q9: It takes the production lock and checks the window. Outside the window it releases the lock, waits for the next window and tries again. If another run holds the production lock, it waits for that lock. A deploy may only start Monday to Thursday, 09:00 to 15:00 UTC.
sonnet.q10: The canary 5xx ratio is measured (5xx requests over all requests for app shop-api-canary, over the last minute) by querying Prometheus. The run checks every 30 seconds for 15 minutes, starting one minute after the rollout. It fails if any sample is above 1% or Prometheus returns no data.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED. The document only says the approval job waits for a release-approvers member and that CI records who approved and when. How approvers are notified and what information they see is not described.
sonnet.q12: It is not rolled back automatically. In staging, a failed deploy ends the run and is announced. In production, the run calls canary-off, releases the lock, fails and announces. The reason is that deploy.sh writes tags only after success, so previous_tag would name an older image than the one running (Kubernetes keeps serving from the old pods and current_tag still names the last good image). A person decides what to do next in production. How staging is returned to a known image is not stated beyond that.
